notes: The page text says pin 4, but the schematic image draws the button/resistor node on pin 2. I used pin 4 because the text is explicit and the sketch uses it.
The tutorial gives no breadboard layout. I placed the button across the centre gap: side 1 (1.l, 1.r) in the top half, columns 10 and 12, and side 2 (2.l, 2.r) in the bottom half, same columns.
5V goes to the button's side 1 (column 10 top). Pin 4 and the 10k resistor share side 2 (column 10 bottom). The resistor's other end is in column 14 bottom, and a wire takes that column to GND.
The 10k resistor is the pull-down: it joins pin 4 to GND. Pressing the button joins 5V to pin 4.
A USB cable is used only to power and program the board, and it is not in the hardware list, so it is not a node.
The breadboard and the three jumper wires are not in the tutorial's hardware list. I added them because the circuit needs a way to join the button, resistor and board pins.
